metadata.title: Mastering the Game of Go with Deep Neural Networks and Tree Search
metadata.authors: Silver, Huang, Maddison, Guez, Sifre, et al.
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Alternating Markov Game
nodes.statement: Two-player game with state space $\mathcal{S}$, action space $\mathcal{A}(s)$, deterministic transition $f(s,a)$, and reward $r_i(s)$, restricted to two-player zero-sum: $r_1(s) = -r_2(s) = r(s)$ with zero rewards except at terminal step $T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two-player zero-sum game with deterministic transitions and reward only at the terminal state.

nodes.name: Policy
nodes.statement: A policy $p(a \mid s)$ is a probability distribution over legal actions $a \in \mathcal{A}(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: A probability distribution over legal actions in each state.

nodes.name: Value Function under Policy $p$
nodes.statement: $v^p(s) = \mathbb{E}[z_t \mid s_t = s, a_{t \ldots T} \sim p]$, the expected terminal outcome when both players follow policy $p$.
nodes.statement_clean: Expected game outcome from state $s$ when both players follow policy $p$.

nodes.name: Optimal Value Function $v^*(s)$
nodes.statement: Unique value function determining the outcome from state $s$ under perfect play: $v^*(s) = z_T$ if $s = s_T$, else $v^*(s) = \max_a -v^*(f(s,a))$.
nodes.statement_clean: The minimax value of a state under optimal play by both players.

nodes.name: SL Policy Network $p_\sigma$
nodes.statement: A 13-layer convolutional neural network $p_\sigma(a \mid s)$ with weights $\sigma$ that alternates convolutional layers with rectifier nonlinearities and outputs a softmax probability distribution over legal moves on the $19 \times 19$ board.
nodes.statement_clean: Deep CNN trained by supervised learning to predict expert human moves.

nodes.name: Fast Rollout Policy $p_\pi$
nodes.section: Supervised learning of policy networks / Methods: Rollout policy
nodes.statement: Linear softmax policy $p_\pi(a \mid s)$ over local 3x3 pattern features and 12-point diamond response patterns, achieving ~24.2% expert-move accuracy in ~2 microseconds per move.
nodes.statement_clean: Fast linear policy used for Monte Carlo rollouts during MCTS.

nodes.name: RL Policy Network $p_\rho$
nodes.statement: Policy network with weights $\rho$ identical in structure to $p_\sigma$ and initialized to $\rho = \sigma$, then improved by self-play policy gradient against randomly sampled previous iterations.
nodes.statement_clean: Policy network refined by self-play reinforcement learning to maximize game-winning probability.

nodes.name: Value Network $v_\theta$
nodes.statement: Convolutional network $v_\theta(s)$ with similar architecture to the policy network but with a single scalar tanh output, approximating $v^{p_\rho}(s) \approx v^*(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Deep CNN that predicts the probability of winning from a board position.

nodes.name: Tree Policy $p_\tau$
nodes.statement: Policy similar to the rollout policy $p_\pi$ but with more features, used to provide placeholder prior probabilities for newly expanded tree nodes before the SL policy network evaluation completes.
nodes.statement_clean: Auxiliary policy that supplies placeholder priors at newly expanded MCTS nodes.

nodes.name: Edge Statistics $(P, N_v, N_r, W_v, W_r, Q)$
nodes.statement: Each search-tree edge $(s,a)$ stores $\{P(s,a), N_v(s,a), N_r(s,a), W_v(s,a), W_r(s,a), Q(s,a)\}$: prior probability, value- and rollout-visit counts, accumulated value-net and rollout values, and the combined mean action value $Q$.
nodes.statement_clean: Statistics maintained at each MCTS edge: prior, two visit counts, two cumulative values, and combined mean action value.

nodes.name: Combined Action Value $Q(s,a)$
nodes.statement: $Q(s,a) = (1-\lambda)\, W_v(s,a)/N_v(s,a) + \lambda\, W_r(s,a)/N_r(s,a)$, a weighted average of value-network and rollout estimates with mixing parameter $\lambda$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mixed action-value estimate combining value-network output and Monte Carlo rollout returns.

nodes.name: Leaf Evaluation $V(s_L)$
nodes.section: Searching with policy and value networks
nodes.statement: $V(s_L) = (1-\lambda)\, v_\theta(s_L) + \lambda\, z_L$, mixing the value-network estimate with a fast-rollout outcome from leaf $s_L$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mixture of value-network output and rollout outcome at a freshly expanded leaf.

nodes.name: SL Policy Gradient Update
nodes.statement: $\Delta \sigma \propto \partial \log p_\sigma(a \mid s) / \partial \sigma$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stochastic gradient ascent on log-likelihood of human moves.

nodes.name: REINFORCE Policy Gradient Update
nodes.statement: $\Delta \rho \propto (\partial \log p_\rho(a_t \mid s_t) / \partial \rho)\, z_t$.
nodes.statement_clean: Policy-gradient update weighted by terminal game outcome.

nodes.name: Value Network MSE Update
nodes.statement: $\Delta \theta \propto (\partial v_\theta(s) / \partial \theta)(z - v_\theta(s))$, minimizing mean squared error between predicted value and observed game outcome.
nodes.statement_clean: Stochastic gradient descent on MSE between predicted value and outcome.

nodes.name: PUCT Action-Selection Bonus
nodes.statement: $u(s,a) = c_{puct}\, P(s,a)\, \sqrt{\sum_b N_r(s,b)} / (1 + N_r(s,a))$, with selection rule $a_t = \arg\max_a (Q(s_t,a) + u(s_t,a))$.
nodes.statement_clean: Variant of PUCT bonus encouraging exploration of high-prior, low-visit moves.

nodes.name: MCTS Convergence to Optimal Value
nodes.statement: Under MCTS with UCT-style action selection, the simulation-policy value converges to the optimal value: $\lim_{n\to\infty} V^n(s) = \lim_{n\to\infty} v^{P^n}(s) = v^*(s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotic convergence of MCTS value estimates to the minimax optimal value.
assumptions: Two-player zero-sum game with finite state and action spaces
MCTS with UCT-style search-control function $\arg\max_a (Q^n(s,a) + u(s,a))$

nodes.name: Supervised Learning of SL Policy Network
nodes.statement: Asynchronous SGD that maximizes log-likelihood of expert moves to train $p_\sigma$ on 30M positions from the KGS Go Server.
input: Augmented KGS data set $\{s^k, a^k\}_{k=1}^m$ (29.4M positions, 8 reflections/rotations)
13-layer CNN architecture with $k=192$ filters
Step size $\alpha = 0.003$ (halved every 80M steps)
Mini-batch size $m=16$
nodes.pseudocode: Repeat for 340M steps: sample mini-batch from KGS; compute $\Delta\sigma = (\alpha/m)\sum_k \partial \log p_\sigma(a^k \mid s^k)/\partial\sigma$; apply asynchronously across 50 GPUs; halve $\alpha$ every 80M steps.

nodes.name: Reinforcement Learning of RL Policy Network
nodes.statement: Self-play policy-gradient training of $p_\rho$ by REINFORCE with baseline against a pool of previous opponents.
input: SL policy network $p_\sigma$ used as initialization $\rho = \rho^- = \sigma$
Pool of past opponent parameters $\rho^-$
Baseline $v(s_t)$ (value network on second pass)
nodes.pseudocode: For 10,000 mini-batches of 128 self-play games: sample opponent $\rho^-$ from pool; play games to termination scoring $z^i_t$; update $\Delta\rho = \alpha \sum_i \sum_t (\partial \log p_\rho(a^i_t \mid s^i_t)/\partial\rho)(z^i_t - v(s^i_t))$; every 500 iterations append current $\rho$ to opponent pool.

nodes.name: Value Network Regression
nodes.statement: MSE-regression training of $v_\theta$ on 30M decorrelated self-play positions, each drawn from a unique game.
input: Self-play data set of 30M (state, outcome) pairs $(s, z)$
Each game generated by sampling $U \sim \mathrm{unif}\{1,450\}$, playing $t < U$ with $p_\sigma$, $a_U \sim \mathrm{unif}\{1,361\}$, then $t > U$ with $p_\rho$
Mini-batch size 32
nodes.pseudocode: For 50M mini-batches across 50 GPUs: sample $\{s^k, z^k\}$; compute $\Delta\theta = (\alpha/m)\sum_k (z^k - v_\theta(s^k))\, \partial v_\theta(s^k)/\partial\theta$; train for ~1 week.

nodes.name: APV-MCTS (Asynchronous Policy and Value MCTS)
nodes.statement: Asynchronous multi-threaded MCTS that combines policy and value networks via four stages (Selection, Expansion, Evaluation, Backup).
input: Root state $s$ of search
SL policy network $p_\sigma$, RL value network $v_\theta$, fast rollout policy $p_\pi$, tree policy $p_\tau$
Parameters $\beta = 0.67$, $\lambda = 0.5$, $n_{vl} = 3$, $n_{thr} = 40$, $c_{puct} = 5$
Computation budget (e.g. 5 s per move; $n$ simulations per second)
output: Selected action $a^* = \arg\max_a N_r(s_{root}, a)$ (most-visited move from root)
nodes.pseudocode: While time remains, run simulations in parallel across CPU/GPU threads; each simulation: 1) Selection (descend tree by $a_t = \arg\max_a (Q + u)$ until leaf $s_L$); 2) Evaluation (queue $s_L$ for value network and run a rollout with $p_\pi$ to terminal); 3) Backup (apply virtual loss; on completion update $N_r, W_r, N_v, W_v, Q$); 4) Expansion (when $N_r(s,a) > n_{thr}$, add successor and set $P \leftarrow p_\sigma^\beta(\cdot \mid s')$). Return $\arg\max_a N_r$ at the root.

nodes.name: Distributed APV-MCTS
nodes.statement: Distributed variant of APV-MCTS with a master holding the search tree, remote worker CPUs running rollouts, and remote worker GPUs evaluating policy/value networks asynchronously.
input: Master machine storing the search tree
Worker CPUs (up to 1202) executing asynchronous rollouts
Worker GPUs (up to 176) evaluating policy and value networks
output: Selected action $a^*$ at the root, as in single-machine APV-MCTS
nodes.pseudocode: Master executes only the in-tree phase; communicates leaf positions to worker CPUs (rollouts) and worker GPUs (network evaluations); workers return rollout outcomes and network outputs which the master backs up along the originating path; placeholder priors at newly expanded nodes are atomically replaced once policy network outputs return.

nodes.name: Cached-Move Rollout Heuristic
nodes.statement: Caches each tree-traversal move in a hash table keyed by 3x3 pattern context; during rollouts, if the current pattern matches, the cached move is played with high probability (a generalization of the 'last good reply' heuristic).
input: Hash table of (pattern context $\to$ stored move) populated during MCTS tree traversal
Current 3x3 pattern context (colour, liberty, stone counts) at each rollout step
output: Move selected for the current rollout step (cached if a context match exists, else $p_\pi$ sample)
nodes.pseudocode: During tree traversal: insert (3x3 context $\to$ most-probable action) into hash table. During rollout: look up current context; on hit, play stored move with high probability; on miss, sample from $p_\pi$.

nodes.name: Symmetry Ensemble for Network Evaluation
nodes.statement: At evaluation time, transforms a position $s$ via the dihedral group $\{d_1, \ldots, d_8\}$ of eight reflections/rotations and averages outputs (explicit) or selects one orientation per evaluation (implicit, used inside APV-MCTS).
input: Position $s$
Dihedral-group transformations $d_1(s), \ldots, d_8(s)$
output: Ensembled value $v_\theta(s) = (1/8)\sum_{j=1}^{8} v_\theta(d_j(s))$ (explicit) or single-orientation evaluation $v_\theta(d_j(s_L))$ for randomly sampled $j$ (implicit)

nodes.name: Alpha-Beta Pruning
nodes.statement: Depth-first minimax tree search with alpha-beta pruning truncated by an approximate value function; achieved superhuman performance in chess, checkers, othello, but not Go.

nodes.name: UCT (Upper Confidence Bounds for Trees)
nodes.statement: MCTS with UCB1-style action selection: $a_t = \arg\max_a (Q^n(s,a) + u(s,a))$, converging asymptotically to the optimal value function.

nodes.name: Pachi (Baseline Go Program)
nodes.statement: Open-source MCTS-based Go program ranked at 2 amateur dan on KGS, executing 100,000 simulations per move; used as a baseline against the RL policy network.

nodes.name: Computer Go: Position Evaluation and Move Selection
nodes.statement: Play Go at superhuman level despite enormous search space (branching $b \approx 250$, depth $d \approx 150$); requires effective approximation $v(s) \approx v^*(s)$ and a sampling policy $p(a \mid s)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Build a Go program that plays at the level of human professionals.

nodes.name: Strength of Policy Networks vs Training Accuracy (Fig. 2a)
nodes.statement: Plot of AlphaGo win rate vs SL policy network training accuracy on KGS, for networks with 128/192/256/384 filters; small accuracy gains yield large strength gains. SL network reached 57.0% expert-move accuracy.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical demonstration that policy-network accuracy correlates strongly with playing strength.

nodes.name: Value Network vs Rollouts Position Evaluation (Fig. 2b)
nodes.statement: Comparison of MSE between predicted value and game outcome across game stages: $v_\theta$ is consistently more accurate than rollouts with $p_\pi$ and approaches accuracy of rollouts with $p_\rho$ at $\sim 1/15{,}000$ the compute.
nodes.statement_clean: Empirical demonstration that the value network matches RL-policy rollouts at a fraction of the cost.

nodes.name: Tournament: AlphaGo vs Other Go Programs (Fig. 4a)
nodes.section: Evaluating the playing strength of AlphaGo
nodes.statement: Internal tournament with 5 s/move: single-machine AlphaGo (Elo 2890) and distributed AlphaGo (Elo 3140) defeated Crazy Stone, Zen, Pachi, Fuego, GnuGo; AlphaGo won 494/495 (99.8%) games against other programs.
nodes.statement_clean: Tournament showing AlphaGo dominates all prior Go programs.

nodes.name: Component Ablation Study (Fig. 4b, ED Table 7)
nodes.section: Evaluating the playing strength of AlphaGo
nodes.statement: AlphaGo variants with $\lambda = 0$ (value only), $\lambda = 1$ (rollouts only), and $\lambda = 0.5$ (mixed): mixed evaluation wins $\geq 95\%$ against single-method variants.
nodes.statement_clean: Ablation showing the mixture of value network and rollouts outperforms either alone.

nodes.name: Hardware Scalability of MCTS (Fig. 4c, ED Table 8)
nodes.section: Evaluating the playing strength of AlphaGo
nodes.statement: Elo rating as a function of search threads (1 to 64) and GPUs (1 to 280); distributed AlphaGo with 64 threads/280 GPUs achieves Elo 3168.
nodes.statement_clean: Scalability study: AlphaGo strength scales with parallelism in CPUs and GPUs.

nodes.name: Match against Fan Hui (European Go Champion)
nodes.section: Evaluating the playing strength of AlphaGo
nodes.statement: Five-game formal match (5-9 October 2015): distributed AlphaGo defeated Fan Hui (2 dan professional) 5-0; first time a computer defeated a human professional Go player at full board without handicap.
nodes.statement_clean: Historic match: AlphaGo beats a human Go professional 5-0.

nodes.name: Move-Selection Visualization (Fig. 5)
nodes.section: Searching with policy and value networks
nodes.statement: Visualization of how AlphaGo selected its move in an informal game vs Fan Hui: value-network estimates $v_\theta(s')$, action values $Q(s,a)$ at $\lambda=0$ and $\lambda=1$, raw SL policy $p_\sigma$, simulation frequencies, and principal variation.
nodes.statement_clean: Visualization of AlphaGo's internal evaluations during a real game position.

nodes.name: SL Policy Better than RL Policy in MCTS
nodes.section: Searching with policy and value networks
nodes.statement: The SL policy network $p_\sigma$ performed better than the stronger RL policy $p_\rho$ as the prior in MCTS, presumably because humans select a diverse beam of promising moves whereas RL optimizes for the single best move.
nodes.statement_clean: Diverse expert priors outperform sharp self-play priors inside MCTS.

nodes.name: RL-derived Value Network Outperforms SL-derived
nodes.section: Searching with policy and value networks
nodes.statement: $v_\theta \approx v^{p_\rho}$ derived from the RL policy performed better in AlphaGo than $v_\theta \approx v^{p_\sigma}$ derived from the SL policy.
nodes.statement_clean: Stronger underlying policy yields a more useful value-network target.

nodes.name: Avoiding Overfitting via Self-Play Data Set
nodes.statement: Training $v_\theta$ on complete KGS games causes overfitting (test MSE 0.37, train MSE 0.19); training instead on 30M decorrelated self-play positions (one per game) yields train MSE 0.226 and test MSE 0.234.
nodes.statement_clean: Decorrelating training positions across distinct games eliminated value-network overfitting.

nodes.name: Symmetries Hurt Large Networks
nodes.statement: Rotationally and reflectionally invariant filters help small networks but hurt large networks because they prevent intermediate filters from identifying specific asymmetric patterns; AlphaGo therefore exploits symmetries only at run-time via dihedral ensembling.
nodes.statement_clean: Dihedral-invariant filters degrade large CNNs; only run-time ensembling is used.

nodes.name: AlphaGo Parameters Used in Match
nodes.statement: Match parameters: softmax temperature $\beta = 0.67$; mixing $\lambda = 0.5$; virtual loss $n_{vl} = 3$; expansion threshold $n_{thr} = 40$; exploration constant $c_{puct} = 5$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hyperparameter values used by the match version of AlphaGo.

nodes.name: Selection
nodes.statement: From the root, descend the tree by selecting at each step $a_t = \arg\max_a (Q(s_t,a) + u(s_t,a))$ with $u(s,a) = c_{puct} P(s,a) \sqrt{\sum_b N_r(s,b)} / (1 + N_r(s,a))$ until reaching a leaf $s_L$ at depth $L$.

nodes.name: Evaluation (Value Network + Rollout)
nodes.statement: Queue $s_L$ for asynchronous evaluation by $v_\theta$; in parallel run a rollout with $p_\pi$ until terminal step $T$, scoring $z_t = \pm r(s_T)$.

nodes.name: Backup with Virtual Loss
nodes.statement: Apply virtual loss on descent ($N_r \mathrel{+}= n_{vl}$, $W_r \mathrel{-}= n_{vl}$). On rollout completion, replace virtual losses with the outcome ($N_r \mathrel{+}= 1 - n_{vl}$, $W_r \mathrel{+}= n_{vl} + z_t$). On value-network completion, update $N_v \mathrel{+}= 1$, $W_v \mathrel{+}= v_\theta(s_L)$.

nodes.name: Expansion
nodes.statement: When $N_r(s,a) > n_{thr}$, add successor $s' = f(s,a)$ to the tree initialized with placeholder priors from $p_\tau$; queue $s'$ for asynchronous SL-policy evaluation; on completion atomically replace priors with $P(s',a) \leftarrow p_\sigma^\beta(a \mid s')$. The threshold $n_{thr}$ is dynamically adjusted to match policy-queue rate to GPU capacity.

nodes.name: Final Move Selection
nodes.statement: After search budget is exhausted, return $a^* = \arg\max_a N_r(s_{root}, a)$ (most-visited child); resign if $\max_a Q(s,a) < -0.8$.

nodes.name: Initialize Self-Play Pool
nodes.statement: Initialize $\rho = \rho^- = \sigma$ (RL weights start from SL); maintain a pool of past opponent parameter snapshots $\rho^-$ for self-play sampling.

nodes.name: Self-Play Game Loop
nodes.statement: For each iteration play $n=128$ games in parallel between $p_\rho$ and a randomly sampled $p_{\rho^-}$ until termination, scoring $z^i_t = \pm r(s_{T_i})$.

nodes.name: REINFORCE Update with Baseline
nodes.statement: Replay games to compute the policy-gradient update $\Delta\rho = \alpha \sum_{i=1}^{n} \sum_{t=1}^{T_i} (\partial \log p_\rho(a^i_t \mid s^i_t)/\partial\rho)(z^i_t - v(s^i_t))$ with $v(s) = v_\theta(s)$ on the second pass.

nodes.name: Append to Opponent Pool
nodes.statement: Every 500 iterations, snapshot the current parameters $\rho$ and add to the opponent pool to stabilize training and prevent overfitting to the current policy.

nodes.name: Generate Decorrelated Self-Play Position
nodes.statement: Sample $U \sim \mathrm{unif}\{1,450\}$; play $t=1,\ldots,U-1$ with $a_t \sim p_\sigma(\cdot \mid s_t)$; play $a_U \sim \mathrm{unif}\{1,361\}$ (resampled until legal); play $t = U+1, \ldots, T$ with $a_t \sim p_\rho(\cdot \mid s_t)$.

nodes.name: Score Game and Add Single Sample
nodes.statement: Score the game to obtain $z_t = \pm r(s_T)$; add only the single training pair $(s_{U+1}, z_{U+1})$ to the data set, providing an unbiased sample of $v^{p_\rho}(s_{U+1})$.

nodes.name: MSE Gradient Update
nodes.statement: For each mini-batch of 32 positions, compute $\Delta\theta = (\alpha/m) \sum_{k=1}^m (z^k - v_\theta(s^k))\, \partial v_\theta(s^k)/\partial\theta$; train for 50M mini-batches across 50 GPUs (~1 week).
